The input runs 2 jobs in turn, each started by --Link1--.

  • Jobs 1 and 2 read the checkpoints earlier jobs left.

System

Symmetry and electrons of the system.

Electron counts and spin follow from the nuclear charges and the charge q:

N_\alpha+N_\beta=\sum_A Z_A-q,\qquad M_S=\frac{N_\alpha-N_\beta}{2},\qquad 2S+1=N_\alpha-N_\beta+1

SCF

Orbitals

HOMO, LUMO and their gap, which is not an excitation energy:

\Delta\epsilon=\epsilon_{\mathrm{LUMO}}-\epsilon_{\mathrm{HOMO}}

Levels near the gap, one column per symmetry:

  • Hover a level to name it; click it to highlight it.
  • The molecule has no symmetry, point group C_1, so orbitals are named from the frontier: \mathrm{HOMO}_{n} below the highest occupied and \mathrm{LUMO}_{n} above the lowest unoccupied.
  • Surfaces hold 85\,\% of \int\psi^2\,\mathrm{d}V; the overall sign is arbitrary.
  • Parts by angular momentum l or atom A, with Mulliken shares summing to 100\,\%.

Properties

Mulliken charges of the final geometry, red q_A<0 and blue q_A>0, comparable only within one method and basis:

Dipole moment, in the printed orientation:

\boldsymbol{\mu}=\begin{pmatrix}5.577 \\ 8.0169 \\ 0.292\end{pmatrix}\,\mathrm{D}=\begin{pmatrix}2.19416 \\ 3.15409 \\ 0.114882\end{pmatrix}\,e a_0,\qquad |\boldsymbol{\mu}|=9.7703\,\mathrm{D}=3.84393\,e a_0

States

Excited states

The job solved for 10 excited states. Each state at its wavelength \lambda_n with oscillator strength f_n, over ultraviolet bands.

Oscillator strength measures the transition dipole moment \boldsymbol\mu_{0n} between the ground state and state n, the matrix element of the dipole operator \hat{\boldsymbol\mu}=-\sum_i\hat{\mathbf r}_i (atomic units):

f_n=\frac{2}{3}\,\Delta E_n\,\lvert\boldsymbol\mu_{0n}\rvert^2,\qquad \boldsymbol\mu_{0n}=\langle\Psi_0|\hat{\boldsymbol\mu}|\Psi_n\rangle=-\int\mathbf r\,\rho_{0n}(\mathbf r)\,\mathrm{d}\mathbf r

Without the symmetry of the states, only f_n tells bright states from dark ones.

Each bar stacks one state’s transition weights w=\sum 2c_{ia}^2, c_{ia}^2 per spin when unrestricted; amplitudes below 0.1 are not printed, and dark states, f<0.001, are faded. - The molecule has no symmetry, point group C_1, so orbitals are named from the frontier: \mathrm{HOMO}_{n} below the highest occupied and \mathrm{LUMO}_{n} above the lowest unoccupied.

Transition orbitals

Orbitals contributing at least 10\,\mathrm{\%} to a state; orange and teal mark the two phases at \pm\psi_0, holding 85\,\% of \int\psi^2\,\mathrm{d}V.

Density changes

By state, degenerate states grouped: blue \Delta\rho<-\Delta\rho_0 where electrons leave, red \Delta\rho>+\Delta\rho_0 where they arrive, holding 80\,\% of \int\lvert\Delta\rho\rvert\,\mathrm{d}V; amplitudes below 0.1 are left out.

Hole and particle densities, one electron each, degenerate states averaged; q_{\mathrm{CT}}, d_{\mathrm{CT}} and S_{\mathrm{hp}} measure transferred charge, centroid distance and overlap:

\rho_{\mathrm{h}}=\frac{\sum_{ij}(\mathbf{X}\mathbf{X}^{\mathsf{T}})_{ij}\,\phi_i\phi_j}{\operatorname{tr}\mathbf{X}\mathbf{X}^{\mathsf{T}}},\qquad \rho_{\mathrm{p}}=\frac{\sum_{ab}(\mathbf{X}^{\mathsf{T}}\mathbf{X})_{ab}\,\phi_a\phi_b}{\operatorname{tr}\mathbf{X}^{\mathsf{T}}\mathbf{X}},\qquad \Delta\rho=\rho_{\mathrm{p}}-\rho_{\mathrm{h}}

q_{\mathrm{CT}}=\int\rho_{+}\,\mathrm{d}\mathbf{r},\qquad d_{\mathrm{CT}}=\lvert\mathbf{R}_{+}-\mathbf{R}_{-}\rvert,\qquad S_{\mathrm{hp}}=\int\sqrt{\rho_{\mathrm{h}}\rho_{\mathrm{p}}}\,\mathrm{d}\mathbf{r}

Natural transition orbitals

NoteFindings
Kind Message

NTOs

Natural transition orbitals

The dominant pair, chosen in the snapshot selector: the hole \phi_{\mathrm{h}} the electron leaves and the particle \phi_{\mathrm{p}} it enters, weighted by \lambda. Orange and teal mark the two phases at \pm\phi_0, holding 85\,\% of \int\phi^2\,\mathrm{d}V.

Transition density

Hole and particle densities from the NTO pairs weighted by \lambda_k, one electron each:

\rho_{\mathrm{h}}=\frac{\sum_k\lambda_k\lvert\phi_{\mathrm{h},k}\rvert^2}{\sum_k\lambda_k},\qquad \rho_{\mathrm{p}}=\frac{\sum_k\lambda_k\lvert\phi_{\mathrm{p},k}\rvert^2}{\sum_k\lambda_k}

The viewer opens on the unrelaxed \Delta\rho=\rho_{\mathrm{p}}-\rho_{\mathrm{h}}, exact within TDA: blue where electrons leave, red where they arrive, holding 80\,\% of each density’s \int\lvert f\rvert\,\mathrm{d}V.

Charge-transfer descriptors use the positive and negative parts of \Delta\rho.

Atomic charge changes from \Delta\rho: red gains electrons, blue loses them.
